summary: Anthropic launched Claude Science, a beta AI workbench app that lets Claude coordinate multi-agent, tool-connected research workflows (data analysis, figure generation, compute job management) for scientists across biology, genomics and chemistry domains.

mechanisms.reason: The product is built around a coordinating agent that spawns and delegates to specialist sub-agents to perform end-to-end research tasks in place of manual tool use.
mechanisms.quote: Users interact with a generalist coordinating agent with access to over 60 curated skills and connectors pre-configured for genomics, single-cell, proteomics, structural biology, cheminformatics, and more. These agents can spin up others and engage with specialist agents created by users.

practices.reason: The actor-critic, coordinator/sub-agent, and forkable-session design is a concrete multi-agent pattern a team could adapt, though the reported gains come from Anthropic's own product setting.
practices.quote: A key component of the workflow, enabled by Claude Science, is the use of actor-critic pairs: one agent creates content while a separate reviewer agent evaluates it for accuracy and citation fidelity.

practices.reason: A reviewer-agent pattern that checks citations, calculations and code-figure consistency is a transferable monitoring/verification method worth evaluating for our own pipelines.
practices.quote: As the pipeline runs, a reviewer agent inspects the outputs, flagging incorrect citations, untraceable numbers, and figures that don’t match their underlying code, and self-correcting as it goes.

practices.reason: Teams working in life sciences would need to account for new connector/skill integrations across dozens of scientific databases and toolkits like BioNeMo.
practices.quote: Claude Science uses the skills in NVIDIA’s BioNeMo Agent Toolkit to connect natively to the life sciences models and libraries in BioNeMo , including Evo 2, Boltz-2, and OpenFold3.
